title: 'Reagan' star Lesley-Anne Down relives 3 terrifying brushes with death: ‘I should have been killed’
summary: Lesley-Anne Down recalls three harrowing brushes with danger, including a chilling link to the Moors murders and a terrifying fake taxi escape.
story: The producer shared the lesson he learned from Ronald Reagan that he has tried to apply to his own life.
Lesley-Anne Down believes she's already used up three of her nine lives.
The actress, who takes on the Iron Lady opposite Dennis Quaid in "Reagan," has shown plenty of steel off-screen, recalling "three times in my life when I should have been killed by other people."
For Down, known for her roles in "North and South" and "Upstairs, Downstairs," the unsettling experiences began when she was just 10 years old.
MORGAN FAIRCHILD SAYS TWO MEN ONCE ABDUCTED HER OFF NYC STREET AS BYSTANDERS LAUGHED
Actress Lesley-Anne Down plays former U.K. Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher in the biopic "Reagan." (Rawhide Pictures)

"I remember there was a little girl, one of a number of children who were murdered and buried on the moors in England," the British star told Fox News Digital. "There was a little girl who had dark hair and blue eyes and was my age, 10. Her name was Leslie Ann Downey. My mother got phone calls when this little girl's identity was announced."

"It wasn't me, of course," said Down. "But it certainly freaked her out. Leslie Ann Downey was about six months younger than me. It turned out there were two people, a man and a woman. Ian Brady and Myra Hindley. They were the killers."
Lesley Ann Downey, age 10, one of the children murdered by Ian Brady and Myra Hindley, is shown in a photo. (Mirrorpix via Getty Images)

Brady and Hindley murdered five children between 1963 and 1965, with several of their victims buried on Saddleworth Moor in northern England, according to The Associated Press. The case became known as the Moors murders.
WATCH: ‘REAGAN’ PRODUCER SHARES WHAT HE LEARNED FROM RESEARCHING RONALD REAGAN

Hindley and Brady were arrested in 1965 and later convicted of murders connected to the case. The five victims were Downey, Pauline Reade, John Kilbride, Keith Bennett and Edward Evans, who ranged in age from 10 to 17. Bennett's body has never been found.
Ian Brady and Myra Hindley were found guilty of murder in Chester, England, on May 6, 1966. Both were sentenced to life imprisonment. (Bettmann Archive)
According to accounts of the case, Downey was abducted after Hindley asked her to help carry packages to a car.
Hindley died in 2002 while serving a life sentence. Brady died in a psychiatric hospital in 2017.

Floral tributes overlook Saddleworth Moor in Saddleworth, United Kingdom, where the body of missing Keith Bennett may be buried. Bennett was abducted by moors murderers Ian Brady and Myra Hindley on June 16, 1964, and they never disclosed his burial location. (Getty Images)
The case frightened Down’s family. But it wouldn’t be the last time danger came close to home.

"A year later, my mother and I were coming back from the launderette with the washing," Down said. "I ran ahead. I left the washing, I left my mother and just ran ahead. I ran uphill and then over a footbridge. As I ran over the footbridge, a man came from the other side. He's walking towards me. He stops in the middle of the footbridge and says, 'Hello.' He then was going to put me in his car."
Harrison Ford and Lesley-Anne Down on the set of "Hanover Street," written and directed by Peter Hyams. (Corbis via Getty Images)

"He told me he needed a babysitter, and he would call my parents when we got to his house," Down said. "I remember having one foot in the car. Seeing my mother broke the spell. Then he was gone. But I still remember that horrible feeling swooping in before my mother came."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
English actress Lesley-Anne Down took on the role of Margaret Thatcher in the 2024 biopic "Reagan." (BSR Agency)
Years later, when Down was 18, she ordered a taxi. But when a car pulled up in the countryside, she climbed in and quickly noticed something was wrong.

"As soon as he's driving away, I'm already feeling that horrible feeling," Down said. "I looked around and there were no radios or anything, like a taxi is supposed to have. So I said, 'Could you pull over, please?' He said, 'Oh no, we don't need to pull over. We'll be there soon.'"
Patrick Swayze and Lesley-Anne Down appear in the TV miniseries "North and South," circa 1985. (Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
Down said she decided to jump from the moving car.
Lesley-Anne Down poses for a portrait in New York circa 1980. (Getty Images)

"I opened the door and threw myself out of the 25-mile an hour car," she said. "I fell onto the curb in a puddle. I was covered in blood. There was nobody around. What did he do? He pulled the car door shut and drove off at top speed. I didn't freeze up because I couldn't. That feeling was familiar to me. I've been through it."

Down, now 72, earned a Golden Globe nomination for her role opposite Patrick Swayze in "North and South." She also starred opposite Peter Sellers in "The Pink Panther Strikes Again" and Harrison Ford in "Hanover Street." She later appeared on the soap opera "The Bold and the Beautiful."
Lesley-Anne Down as Madeline Fabray LaMotte Main in the TV miniseries 'North and South,' 1985. (Getty Images)
When asked what advice she would give to women pursuing a career in Hollywood, Down had a warning: "Never go anywhere alone."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Lesley-Anne Down, a British actress, is pictured at home in Primrose Hill, London, on Wednesday, Oct. 4, 1972. (Getty Images)

"Always have your agent or your publicist with you at all times," she said. "Even if they have to be on the phone a lot and out in the lobby, just always have somebody with you at all times as you chase your dreams."

"I made a decision many, many years ago, actually about 2012, that I wanted out," Down said. "I was in a position where I didn't have to. Things were very good. And I was fortunate to have all my eggs in a basket and make a choice."
Lesley-Anne Down attends the 6,000th episode of "The Bold and the Beautiful" at CBS Television City in Los Angeles on Feb. 7, 2011. (FilmMagic)
Down has since moved from California to Georgia. She also said she has no regrets about turning down two opportunities to play a Bond girl.
Sean Connery and Lesley-Anne Down in a scene from the 1979 film "The Great Train Robbery." (Getty Images)

"I guess my thought process was maybe a little old-fashioned, but being a Bond girl didn't really resonate with me," she explained. "Being a Bond girl was skimpy clothing, pretty face, not much dialogue, no acting involved, kissing James at the end in a spacecraft or whatever. I thought if I became a Bond girl, then I'd be a Bond girl for life. I didn't want that for myself."
The opportunity to play Thatcher came "out of the blue," Down said. She accepted the role and said she was grateful for the experience.
Lesley Anne-Down attends The Hollywood Show held at the Westin LAX Hotel in Los Angeles on Feb. 10, 2018. (WireImage)
"She loved and believed in England and the English people," Down said. "Her counterpart, Mr. Reagan, also believed and loved the American people."

The director's cut of "Reagan" was released on Sept. 25, 2026. (Rawhide Pictures)
Down said leaders should "encompass what Thatcher and Reagan both believed," including doing "anything and everything they can for the longevity and success of the nation."

For Down, taking on the role of Thatcher became another unexpected chapter in a life that has repeatedly taken surprising turns. But these days, the actress is content with where those turns have taken her.

Margaret Thatcher, British Prime Minister, addresses a Press Conference at Conservative Party Headquarters in Smith Square, London on June 8, 1987, during the General Election campaign. (David Levenson/Getty Images)

title: Kelly Clarkson slams Brooklyn store over ‘Pretty Woman’ treatment
summary: Kelly Clarkson claims a Brooklyn store employee treated her like she couldn't afford the merchandise, comparing the experience to "Pretty Woman."
story: Steve Summers, Dolly Parton's creative director, joins Martha MacCallum on 'The Story' to discuss the opening of the 'Life of Many Colors Museum' and hotel in Nashville, Tennessee. The projects celebrate the legendary singer's rags-to-rhinestones legacy. Fans express emotional reactions to the immersive experience, sharing how they can feel her presence throughout the new building.
Kelly Clarkson is calling out a Brooklyn store after she claimed an employee mistreated her.
On Saturday, the singer and talk show host took to X to share details of her recent experience at Art of Play, a store known for its collection of toys, games, books, puzzles and other unique items.

"Just drove all the way to Brooklyn to check out this store I thought looked really rad and had a few things in mind to buy and literally was looked at as if I couldn’t afford it and was told he could find something comparable for me," Clarkson wrote.
KELLY CLARKSON WON’T LET HER KIDS WATCH ‘FROM JUSTIN TO KELLY’ AFTER BRUTAL ADMISSION ABOUT 2003 FILM
Kelly Clarkson described a recent shopping experience to one of Julia Roberts' character in "Pretty Woman." (Getty Images)
"Wow, dude. You’re an idiot and just lost a huge sale," she continued.

Clarkson then compared the encounter to a memorable scene from the 1990 film "Pretty Woman," in which Julia Roberts’ character, Vivian Ward, is dismissed by a boutique saleswoman who assumes she cannot afford the store’s clothing.
MICHAEL DOUGLAS' WILDEST HOLLYWOOD CONFESSIONS: FROM A-LIST ACTRESS BITE TO JULIA ROBERTS CLASH
"But y’all should go check out Art of Play in Brooklyn if you enjoy being treated like Julia Roberts’ character in ‘Pretty Woman.’ For sure, check it out," Clarkson added.
The singer’s description of the incident echoed the famous "Pretty Woman" scene, in which Vivian returns to the boutique after being rejected and tells the saleswoman, "Big mistake. Big. Huge."

Clarkson’s post quickly drew attention from her followers, some of whom defended the singer and criticized the store on social media. Several users also appeared to leave negative reviews on the business’ Google listing.
The singer called out Art of Play in Brooklyn for allegedly mistreating her. (Getty Images for The Rock and Roll Hall of Fame)
KELLY CLARKSON WON’T LET HER KIDS WATCH ‘FROM JUSTIN TO KELLY’ AFTER BRUTAL ADMISSION ABOUT 2003 FILM
One Yelp reviewer wrote, Rude!!!! If I could give zero I would! Treat people like you want to be treated walking into a store."
Art of Play so far has not issued a formal statement addressing Clarkson’s claims.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
However, the store appeared to respond indirectly by sharing an Instagram Story featuring a customer review praising the staff’s "genuine kindness," according to Us Weekly.
"From the very first time I walked into @artofplay, I felt welcomed and treated with such genuine kindness," the review stated.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Clarkson's alleged encounter prompted chatter online. (Weiss Eubanks/NBCUniversal via Getty Images)
The customer added that Art of Play was "a place that leaves you smiling and wanting to come back."
The Instagram Story was later deleted, according to the outlet.
The store posted a statement about Clarkson to their Instagram page on Sunday afternoon.

"Yesterday, Kelly Clarkson visited us in Brooklyn and inquired about buying "Molly," a one-of-a-kind singing and dancing bird automaton who plays an important role in the magic shows we host here. Molly is permanently attached to the wall and isn’t for sale," the store wrote.

Adding: "However, the negative experience Kelly described on twitter would resonate with anyone who has ever felt judged in a shop. At Art of Play whether someone comes in to make a purchase or simply look around for a while, they are equally welcome. We greet everyone who walks in the door with the invitation to "pick things up and play." And they do, many stay for hours enjoying our puzzles, games and toys."

"Imagine our surprise when our small local business was suddenly attacked by 8 million people who have never visited our store. It’s been a surreal experience  to be the focus of such widespread outrage after just one mention by a celebrity. Thanks to all our friends for their support and welcome to all the curious folks who discovered us amidst the drama. We’re going to keep our heads down and hopefully, we can clear things up with Kelly someday. As a talented popular singer once said "what doesn’t kill you makes you stronger."
After the store's Instagram post, Clarkson took to her X account and Instagram stories on Sunday afternoon to respond to their claims.
"Cool, cool. Sure, it wasn't for sale. That's the narrative Art of Play is gonna go with," Clarkson wrote, adding a thumbs up emoji.

The singer continued: "So the whole conversation we had when I asked you if it was for sale whilst pointing to the price tag hanging on the wall with the title Singing Bird didn't happen as you elevator eyed me saying in a condescending tone "yes, it’s for sale but it costs 15,000 dollars so if you’d like me to find something comparable for you I can." That all never happened and now it’s not for sale. Okay, cool. So you’re not only rude, you’re also a liar. Got it," adding a checkmark emoji.

Clarkson added: "And by the way, I obviously support small businesses because I was literally at a small business trying to purchase things. I love small businesses and know they are important and I always support them, but you don’t get a free pass to treat people less than in your store just because you are a small business. It’s not that hard to be kind. I never blast people but you my friend were an exception. Your store is really cool. Unfortunately, you aren’t."

The star also added a photo which included what appeared to be an alleged price tag for the item circled in red. The photo had the caption: "Molly’s not for sale yet has a $15,000 price tag. Kelly Clarkson you will always be a real one."
MICHAEL DOUGLAS' WILDEST HOLLYWOOD CONFESSIONS: FROM A-LIST ACTRESS BITE TO JULIA ROBERTS CLASH
A representative for Art of Play did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

title: Elon Musk's mom Maye nearly turned down SI Swimsuit cover over 'wrinkles and cellulite'
summary: Maye Musk nearly turned down her Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover over wrinkle fears, but a phone call from her daughter changed everything.
story: Author Maye Musk joins Fox & Friends to discuss her new memoir "Timeless." She shares her story of escaping a toxic marriage, raising three children as a single mother and finding career success after 50.
Maye Musk nearly passed on the chance to make a splash in Sports Illustrated Swimsuit because she worried about looking "wrinkly" in the iconic magazine.

The Canadian-born, South African-raised model made history in 2022 as the oldest Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover model at 74. Martha Stewart later broke the record at 81 in 2023. Now, Musk is looking back at the milestone and her journey from a single mother of three to a sought-after model in her new book, "Timeless."

"At my age, you have wrinkles and cellulite on your arms and on your thighs, so I prefer to wear long sleeves," the mother of tech mogul Elon Musk told Fox News Digital. "So, the idea of wearing a swimsuit was very uncomfortable. But then my daughter called me. I told her they were going to be shooting in Belize. She instantly said, 'You've got to go. Belize is beautiful.' So, I did. I took a chance."
MAYE MUSK DEFENDS SYDNEY SWEENEY'S NUDE SPORTS AD AND RECALLS 12-YEAR PATH TO CITIZENSHIP

Canadian-South African model Maye Musk arrives for the screening of the film "Asteroid City" during the 76th edition of the Cannes Film Festival in Cannes, on May 23, 2023. Musk has written a new book, "Timeless." (Patricia De Melo Moreira/AFP via Getty Images)

In the book, Musk wrote, "I was still 73. My skin showed the signs of my weight having cycled up and down so many times in my life, including for each of my pregnancies. I'm wrinkly and I have cellulite. Swimsuit model?"
Despite her worries, Musk said she felt at ease when she began posing for photographer Yu Tsai. She even wore colorful two-pieces for the occasion.
Fox News may be compensated for or earn a commission if you buy through our referral links.
Maye Musk is seen here posing for the 2022 Sports Illustrated swimsuit issue cover on Jan. 29, 2022, in Belize (Yu Tsai/Sports Illustrated via Contour RA by Getty Images)

"It was very unusual," she said with a laugh. "I've been told all of my life that I'm not a swimsuit model. When you think of swimsuit models, you think of the Victoria's Secret models. Those are really special body shapes. So it was a challenge for me. But as I say, you have to take a chance in life. And I knew they're not going to publish ugly photos. At one point, I felt so at ease that I even started dancing with the local people. I was in awe of exploring a new country, a new culture. That's what I love doing. And I got to celebrate me."
WATCH: MAYE MUSK DISCUSSES RAISING ELON MUSK, ESCAPING TOXIC MARRIAGE IN NEW MEMOIR ‘TIMELESS’
Looking back, Musk said she wonders why she was so nervous.

"When women go to the beach, they wrap a towel around themselves," she said. "But men, they could be obese, and they're still strutting in Speedos with such confidence. We really have to make a change. And if any man insults your body, well, they can get lost. There's always going to be somebody who feels the need to trash on you. It's not fair. But it's all about embracing who you are and not apologizing for that."
Maye Musk's book "Timeless: The Art of Reinvention and Resilience at Any Age" is available now. (Harper Wave)
Musk didn't undergo a makeover to appear younger for the cover. Her signature silver hair remained untouched.
Maye Musk attends the launch of the 2025 Sports Illustrated Swimsuit issue at Hard Rock Hotel New York on May 15, 2025, in New York City. (Getty Images for Sports Illustrated Swimsuit)

"Why do I need to color my hair?" Musk said. "You have to do the roots every four weeks, and I used to do them myself. Your hair then becomes very brittle because it's so damaged. And it grows out. And then I decided to cut my hair short. Soon after, I had four billboards in Times Square. I didn't feel like a granny. I felt fashionable."
It wasn't the first time Musk took a chance on a modeling gig.

From left: Christie Brinkley, Maye Musk, Brooks Nader, Kate Love, Kate Upton and Lily Aldridge attend the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Celebration of the 2024 Issue Release and 60th Anniversary with Swimsuit Island in Hollywood, Florida, on May 17, 2024. (Getty Images for Sports Illustrated Swimsuit)
In her book, Musk describes a phone call she received from her agent: "Tomorrow, you pose naked for the cover of TIME magazine. You're the only model they want and they won't budge."
Musk had never done a nude shoot because, as she wrote, "nobody had ever asked."
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Maye Musk, an author and dietician, also has campaigns with high-profiled brands like CoverGirl and Dior Beauty. (Fadil Berisha)
Before stripping down, Musk sought advice from her children.

"I picked up the phone to dial Elon first, then stopped myself," Musk wrote. "I already knew what he would say: 'Absolutely not.' He was not the kind of son who wanted his mother naked on magazine covers. Not prudish, but definitely more conservative when it came to nudity. So I called Tosca. I wasn't too surprised to find that she was not in love with the idea, either. 'You never do naked!' she said. Her instinct was protective, not wanting me to risk an uncomfortable experience."
Maye Musk and Elon Musk attend the 2022 Met Gala celebrating "In America: An Anthology of Fashion" at the Metropolitan Museum of Art on May 2, 2022, in New York City. (Getty Images)

"Finally, I called Kimbal," she wrote. "Of my three children, he is the most relaxed and free-spirited. (He met his current wife at Burning Man.) He had a completely different perspective. ‘It’s TIME magazine. It’s journalism,’ he said. ‘Not some nudie magazine. It’ll be tasteful. You have nothing to worry about. Do it.’"
Musk told Fox News Digital it was important for her to get her children's approval before posing nude.
Maye Musk walks the runway at the Philipp Plein fashion show during Milan Fashion Week Womenswear Fall/Winter 2023/2024 on Feb. 25, 2023, in Milan, Italy. (Getty Images)
"Well, would you want your mother naked on the front cover of a magazine?" she said.

"But it was Kimbal who encouraged me. He said it would be tasteful. He's always been a free spirit. And I trust him. When I arrived for the photoshoot, they were very careful with me. You have a makeup artist who has to go through your whole body. Then they did my hair and very plain makeup. Then they sat me with a mirror in front of me, so I could see exactly what the photographer sees."
From left: Kimbal Musk, his mother Maye Musk and his wife Christiana Musk attend the Kering Foundation Caring For Women Dinner in New York City. (Getty Images)

"The photographer came in for the shoot, and maybe five minutes later, it was over," she said. "It was really quick and very respectful. They immediately brought a robe for me. I got changed and went home. That's all there was to it."
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Maye Musk attends the Sports Illustrated Swim Issue Launch Party at the Hard Rock Hotel on May 16, 2024, in New York. (WWD via Getty Images)

For Musk, aging with confidence isn't just about embracing wrinkles and silver hair. The longtime dietitian also believes that taking care of your health plays an important role in feeling your best at any age.
Maye Musk attends the Juzui FW25 Collection show at The Glasshouse in New York City on Feb. 7, 2025. (Getty Images for Juzui)

"It gets harder to lose weight as you get older," Musk said. "With my patients, I always tell them to plan ahead. If you get hungry, there's no salad next to you. There's a donut. Also, only eat when you're hungry. And when you are hungry, make sure there is healthy food around, no desserts or chocolates. And if my patient didn't take the journey seriously, I would tell them, 'You can't come anymore.'"
From left: Tosca Musk and her mother Maye Maye Musk attend the "Downton Abbey: The Grand Finale" New York premiere at Jazz at Lincoln Center on Sept. 8, 2025. (WireImage)

"Even 10 pounds can make you feel uncomfortable," she said. "Everything is tight and you don't have confidence. You have to track your food intake. If a patient goes off what I recommended, they need to explain why. You need to hold yourself accountable if you want to make smarter choices for your health."
Maye Musk attends the launch of the 2022 Sports Illustrated Swimsuit issue and debut of Pay With Change at Hard Rock Hotel New York on May 19, 2022. (Getty Images)
Musk said each decade of her life has been better than the last. At 78, she's happily embracing aging and hopes other women will do the same.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Maye Musk visits "Fox & Friends" at Fox News Channel Studios in New York City on Sept. 18, 2026. (Getty Images)

"When my mom was 86, she moved from South Africa to Canada and started all over," Musk said. "She was an artist. When she was nearing 90, her hands weren't strong enough to do the wood carvings she loved. So, by 94, she started doing computer art. My older sister taught her. She died at 98. But she always remained curious and busy. She was always exploring."
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

From left: Maye Musk, Christen Harper, Hailey Clauson and Georgina Burke attend the Swimsuit on Location event hosted by Sports Illustrated Swimsuit at Hard Rock Seminole in Hollywood, Florida, on May 21, 2022. (Getty Images for Sports Illustrated Swimsuit)

"You're never too old to start again," Musk said. "And don't worry about the wrinkles. A man doesn't care if he gets wrinkles. He still has his confidence. When you get insecure, you become less attractive. I didn't do anything to my face because I wanted to frown and have expression. But also, don't mix with people who make you feel insecure. They're not your friends. And there will be people who will push you down. You can't stay down. You just have to get up and show your talents, who you are."
Stephanie Nolasco is an Entertainment Reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Prince Edward told girlfriend he wanted 'two wives' before marrying royal family's 'secret weapon': memoir
summary: Ruthie Henshall claims in her memoir that Prince Edward once told her he wished he could have two wives before marrying Sophie, Duchess of Edinburgh.
story: Royal historian Hugo Vickers, who wrote a new book on the late monarch, explains how the Queen Mother favored another suitor, but Queen Elizabeth ultimately chose Prince Philip.
Before Prince Edward married his royal family's "secret weapon," he once told an ex-girlfriend he wished he could have two wives, according to her new memoir.

Years earlier, the youngest son of the late Queen Elizabeth II dated actress Ruthie Henshall from 1988 to 1993. The West End star recently opened up about their romance in her memoir "The Showgirl and the Prince."

"Ruth, I couldn't put you through the job," Henshall recalled Edward telling her. "If I could, I would have two wives. One for the job, and one whom I loved, because you would never want to subject the woman you love to the job."
QUEEN ELIZABETH’S MOTHER WANTED HER TO MARRY ANOTHER MAN BEFORE PRINCE PHILIP: AUTHOR
Prince Edward's former flame, actress Ruthie Henshall, has written a memoir about their past romance. (Max Mumby/Indigo/Getty Images; David M. Benett/Getty Images)
Fox News Digital reached out to Henshall, 59, and Edward, 62, for comment. A Buckingham Palace spokesperson previously told Fox News Digital the palace doesn't comment on books.

The pair first met in 1988 while Henshall was starring in "Cats" and Edward was working as a production assistant for Andrew Lloyd Webber's Really Useful Theatre Company. Henshall recalled making a beeline for the young prince when he arrived at the theater, playfully welcoming him "to the litter." A romance blossomed.
Fox News may be compensated for or earn a commission if you buy through our referral links.
"The Showgirl and the Prince" by Ruthie Henshall is available now. (Macmillan Publishers)
As their relationship grew more serious, Henshall said the realities of royal life began to set in.
WATCH: WHY QUEEN ELIZABETH REJECTED HER MOTHER'S PREFERRED MATCH: AUTHOR

"Honestly, this type of thinking is very standard for royal men throughout history," royal commentator Amanda Matta told Fox News Digital. "It's why royal mistresses were so common. For most of history, official marriages have been strategic and political arrangements. But the royals are still people, and they need intimacy and companionship like anyone else."
"Edward and Sophie have been married for over 25 years though and seem genuinely well-matched," Matta added.
Prince Edward, Duke of Edinburgh and Sophie, Duchess of Edinburgh attend Day 2 of the Royal Windsor Horse Show in Home Park at Windsor Castle in Windsor, England, on May 2, 2024. (Getty Images)
Royal broadcaster Ian Pelham Turner told Fox News Digital it's easy to see why the prince was drawn to Henshall.
Actress Ruthie Henshall poses at a photocall for the Broadway musical "She Loves Me," date unknown. (PA Images via Getty Images)

"Ruthie Henshall has been a renowned theatre actress for several decades and Edward loved that world," he explained. "I personally remember working with the National Youth Music Theatre of which Edward was president, so Ruthie would have been his ideal partner at the time."

"The relationship went on for quite a while, and she was very nervous meeting the royal family, especially the queen," Turner said. "She forgot to curtsy to her. She also saw first-hand how the royal family operated with all their high jinks behind the scenes. I feel, although she felt deeply fond of Edward, she realized she could not marry him and still have her beloved career, which was her main passion."
Prince Edward during the wedding of Prince Andrew and Sarah Ferguson on July 23, 1986, in London. (WireImage)
In the book, Henshall wrote that, at least initially, she believed love might be enough to overcome the rigid expectations of marrying into the royal family.
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE
Ruthie Henshall, as Marguerite, and Julian Ovenden, as Armand, perform in "Marguerite" at the Theatre Royal Haymarket in London. (Corbis via Getty Images)

"Of course, I had spotted some etiquette dilemmas, but typically I'd just assumed that I'd be able to break the rules," Henshall wrote. "That an exception would be made for me. I knew how to be a good girl, but I also knew that the possibility of me going out on a wild night and flashing my boobs in public was quite high. So, there were times when I felt torn about it all, but as far as I was concerned, I just wanted him."
Matta suggested Henshall would have adapted to royal life rather than challenged its traditions.
Diana, Princess of Wales, Prince Charles (left) and Prince Edward (right) visit Wanganui Collegiate in Wanganui, New Zealand, during the Royal Tour of New Zealand on April 22, 1983. (Getty Images)

"I don't think Henshall would have shaken up the institution very much," Matta said. "Growing up British, she would have understood the monarchy and grasped the weight of its traditions in a way a true outsider or foreigner might not. In that sense, she's similar to Edward himself. He has a big personality and a real love of the art world, but he's also deeply dutiful."
Ruthie Henshall is seen here performing on stage. (Redferns)
"I suspect that, if she'd married him, she would have adapted to the role rather than reinvented it. That may have even meant giving up her career, as Sophie later had to do."
Henshall wrote that she even turned to Sarah Ferguson, who was then married to the former Prince Andrew, for guidance.
Sarah Ferguson and Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor are seen here on their wedding day in 1986. (Derek Hudson/Getty Images)
"One time when I was pining for Edward, I remember saying to Sarah, 'Would I ever be allowed to marry him?'" Henshall wrote.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Sarah Ferguson, later Duchess of York, is surrounded by press photographers as she arrives for work in Mayfair, London, on March 3, 1986, shortly after the announcement of her engagement to Prince Andrew. (David Levenson/Getty Images)

"She probably knew there wasn't a chance in hell, but still kindly said she didn't know. Later, in her memoir, she described how she wanted to make any other woman coming into the royal family feel comfortable. And she absolutely did that. She made it her mission. So, I think I got the best side of her. And I was grateful to her on many occasions."

As Henshall's career continued to rise, she realized that she and Edward came from different worlds — worlds that were too different. Unwilling to give up her career for royal life, Henshall knew their relationship wasn't going to work.
Prince Edward is seen here in London, date unknown. (Tim Graham Photo Library via Getty Images)

"We had wanted to be together," Henshall wrote. "We had tried desperately to make it work. But it seemed impossible because of who he was, and what I wanted to do in my career. There was this push–pull going on all the time, and we'd reached a point of no return."
Host Ruthie Henshall performs on stage during "Magic at the Musicals" at the Royal Albert Hall in London on May 4, 2017. (John Phillips/Getty Images)
"... I fell in love with him, and it wasn't because he was a prince. ... But at times, it was only too obvious that we came from different worlds."
Despite the breakup, Turner suggested Edward and Henshall remained close.
Ruthie Henshall attends The Olivier Awards with Mastercard at the Royal Opera House on April 3, 2016, in London, England. (Getty Images)
"As far as I know, their great friendship has remained through the decades," Turner said.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE

The newly-wed British royal couple Prince Edward and Sophie Rhys-Jones greet wellwishers on their way from Windsor Castle after their wedding ceremony on June 19, 1999. The royal couple took a brief ride through the historic town of Windsor. (AFP via Getty Images)
In 1999, Edward married Sophie, who later gave up her public relations career to become a full-time working royal. The couple have two children: Lady Louise, 22, and James, Earl of Wessex, 18.

Edward and Sophie decided not to use prince and princess titles for their children, allowing them to choose whether to use those titles and His or Her Royal Highness (HRH) styling when they turned 18, People magazine reported. Neither has chosen to do so.

Prince Edward, Duke of Edinburgh, James, Earl of Wessex and Lady Louise Windsor watch an RAF flypast from the balcony of Buckingham Palace following the coronation of King Charles III and Queen Camilla at Westminster Abbey in London, England, on May 6, 2023. (Getty Images)

Over the years, Sophie has earned a reputation as one of the royal family's most dedicated and reliable members. She has taken on additional royal duties as King Charles oversees a slimmed-down monarchy and has largely avoided public scandal.

Prince Edward, Duke of Edinburgh and Sophie, Duchess of Edinburgh attend The Royal British Legion's 80th Anniversary of D-Day Service of Remembrance at the National Memorial Arboretum in Alrewas, England, on June 6, 2024. (Getty Images)
"Prince Edward is married to the characterful, dependable, hardworking and personable Duchess Sophie," royal broadcaster and photographer Helena Chard told Fox News Digital.

title: 'Happy Days' star Anson Williams says he had to create a second career because sitcom pay wasn't enough
summary: Anson Williams reveals how conversations with David Cassidy and Barry Williams inspired him to pitch a musical act on the iconic sitcom.
story: ‘Happy Days’ star Anson Williams recalled how the sitcom was facing cancelation before it ‘exploded’ and became the number one most-watched show in America.
When playing Potsie Weber on "Happy Days" didn't pay well enough, actor Anson Williams came up with a side hustle: a music career.
In a recent interview on the "Still Here Hollywood Podcast," the 77-year-old actor revealed the singing sideline was simply a matter of 1970s economics.

"On 'Happy Days' we didn't have the same salaries they have today. Not even close," he said. "Nine hundred dollars an episode, $1,200 an episode. It was fine back then, but...it's not a lifetime of earnings there."

Williams said that after speaking to "Partridge Family" star David Cassidy and Barry Williams, of "The Brady Bunch," about how much money they were making by taking their singing acts off the show, he thought to himself, "Wait a minute. I sing. If I can convince Garry to put a band on the show, maybe I can get booked, and maybe I can get some extra income."
Williams shared he pitched the idea for him to sing on the show in order to make more money. (Michael Buckner/Penske Media via Getty Images)
‘BRADY BUNCH’ CAST MADE NEARLY NOTHING FROM DECADES OF RERUNS, EVE PLUMB CLAIMS

After speaking with the show's creator, Garry Marshall, about the possibility of putting together a band to perform at Arnold's, the burger joint where Fonzie held court, the legendary director gave him a chance. Marshall told him he would have to pick a song and sing it to a bulldog, telling him, "If you're good, I get laughs. If you're bad, I get laughs. You're going to sing the bulldog."

"So I do it and then the letters start coming in, and he goes 'The people like it. The people like it.' He goes, 'We'll do more. You're in charge of it though,'" Williams recalled. "Then I got a major agent for that and started getting booked at state fairs for 10 years."
Williams added that his idea to sing on the show "started this whole career" that ended up being better for him monetarily, and was "just a whole other life experience."

After finding success as a musician as well as an actor, Williams said that Marshall approached him to express how proud he was of the actor, telling him, "You found an opportunity, and you're helping the show."
Williams previously shared with Fox News Digital that the show was on the verge of being cancelled. (ABC Photo Archives/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images)
GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

During an interview with Fox News Digital in March 2024, Williams revealed that while the show started as a hit with audiences, landing in the top 15 or 20, it slid down to 48th place at one point and was "on the verge of getting canceled."

"And Garry Marshall and Jerry Paris, our director, thought, ‘What if we changed the whole tone? What if we make it a live audience sitcom?’" Williams recalled. "So, half the season, one camera. The next season, one camera. The next season — two and a half in — they switch it to live audience. And the chemistry of the cast, the writing, was magic. That's the year we went to No. 1 in the world. That's when we exploded."

When the show became a huge success, Williams recalled Marshall advising him and his young co-stars to use their platforms for good, telling them to take the spotlight they found themselves in and "shine it on people that deserve it."

Following his time on "Happy Days," Williams pivoted to working more as a writer and director. He directed episodes of "Beverly Hills, 90210," "Sabrina the Teenage Witch," "Lizzie McGuire," "Charmed," "The Secret Life of an American Teenager" and more.

Through all his successes, Williams never forgot the advice Marshall gave to him during his time on "Happy Days."

"Ron Howard and I did a film called ‘Skyward,’ starring the first paraplegic ever in the history of television," he said. "We did films like ‘No Greater Gift,’ which doubled organ donorship cards. Henry did so many social issue movies of the week and after-school specials, and charities."

story: Drew Baldridge tells Fox News Digital about Jelly Roll's massive backstage entourage.
Country music superstars may share the spotlight, but their lives behind the scenes can look very different.

Drew Baldridge, who recently released his album, "Farm Faith Family," got a front-row seat to both worlds, from Luke Bryan's down-home lifestyle to Jelly Roll's jam-packed backstage scene, where the next unexpected guest could be just around the corner.

title: Paulina Porizkova's gym routine led to ‘a revelation’ in her 60s
summary: Paulina Porizkova reveals how heavy lifting and Pilates transformed her severe anxiety and strength after bilateral hip replacement surgery.

Paulina Porizkova is enjoying the benefits of exercising after starting to work out.
In a recent Instagram post, the 61-year-old supermodel shared her gym routine with her many followers and said working out has helped her in more ways than one.

"I really used to hate to work out. And, so, I didn’t do it until I was in my 40s, and I realized that it really helped with my pretty severe anxiety," she said in voice-over footage of her lifting weights. "And also it made me look better."
PAULINA PORIZKOVA WOWS IN STRIKING BIKINI WHILE CELEBRATING HER 61ST BIRTHDAY

She explained that while she still doesn't like working out and would "much rather be reclining on the couch and reading novels," that would help "feed my brain, but it doesn’t really do it for my body."
So, she chooses to go to the gym.
Porizkova shared her workout routine on Instagram, letting fans know why she works out. (Stefanie Keenan/Getty Images for Estée Lauder)
The supermodel shared that she tries to go to the gym three days a week, alternating between focusing on her upper body and her lower body, and leaves one day to work both out.
She explained that she's taken the advice of doctors and Instagram influencers and tries "to lift heavy," adding that she also mixes Pilates into her routine.
In the video, Porizkova does exercises such as hammer curls, cable pulls, deadlifts, pull-ups, lunges and others.

"What's wonderful about it is, it not only helps my severe anxiety and makes me look better, but it also has made me a lot stronger," she added. "So, despite my 10-pound weight gain, I can dance the night away with people half my age. How about that?"

title: Michael Douglas' wildest Hollywood confessions: From A-list actress bite to Julia Roberts clash
summary: Michael Douglas alleges a confrontation with Julia Roberts, secret affairs and a cocaine-fueled evening with O.J. Simpson in his new memoir.
story: In his memoir, ‘One Helluva Ride,’ the actor admitted he had an affair with his ‘Basic Instinct’ co-star, Jeanne Tripplehorn. (This video contains AI-assisted content.)
Michael Douglas is pulling back the curtain on the most explosive moments of his life, both in front of the camera and behind the scenes.

In his memoir, "One Helluva Ride," the actor-producer also opens up about secret affairs; heavy cocaine and alcohol use; a "rehab or divorce" ultimatum from his first wife, Diandra; and the painful family struggles that followed him from childhood into fatherhood.

Douglas details his volatile relationship with his late father, Kirk Douglas, his son Cameron’s addiction and imprisonment and the Stage 4 cancer diagnosis that forced him to confront his own mortality.
Michael Douglas's memoir, "One Helluva Ride," was released Oct. 6.  (Getty Images)
Here are the top ten bombshells:
MICHAEL DOUGLAS CONFIRMS SECRET AFFAIR WITH KATHLEEN TURNER ON 'ROMANCING THE STONE' SET
An A-list actress bit him during casting dinner
Debra Winger allegedly bit Michael Douglas in the 1980s. (Getty Images)
In the book, Douglas recalled he and filmmakers were trying to convince Debra Winger to star as Joan Wilder in "Romancing the Stone," but the meeting took an odd turn.

"We took Debra to dinner and, once again, it was an epic meal. Any time you have dinner with Jack or Danny, it’s a riot. … But the real goal of the dinner was to get Debra on board to make Romancing the Stone, and no matter how hard we tried, she would not give us an answer, one way or the other. We were stuck in limbo.
MICHAEL DOUGLAS ADMITS HE ALMOST LEFT HIS WIFE FOR HIS 'BASIC INSTINCT' CO-STAR AFTER AFFAIR

"Stories had filtered back that Debra was delivering an incredible performance in Terms of Endearment, but also that she was difficult during shooting and had huge, blow-out fights with Shirley MacLaine.

"We all left the restaurant and were walking down the street when, the way somebody might punch you in the arm as you part company, Debra leaned over and bit me. I mean, she really bit me. Jesus, I had a whole set of teeth marks dug into my arm. We still had no answer from her, but that bite sealed the deal for me. No, thank you!"
MICHAEL DOUGLAS REVEALS HE MADE FIVE PHONE CALLS TO FIVE WOMEN THE DAY HE CHOSE CATHERINE ZETA-JONES
Douglas said he later reenacted the moment for Fox executives, telling them, "She bit me. Hard. Look at the teeth marks in my arm."
Although the studio pushed back because Winger was a major star, Douglas held his ground. Winger ultimately did not join the project, and Kathleen Turner was cast in the role.
Fox News Digital has reached out to reps for Winger for comment.
Douglas confronted Julia Roberts over his teenage son
Michael Douglas said he once snapped at Julia Roberts while drunk.  (Getty Images)
Douglas experienced another tense moment involving Julia Roberts at a Golden Globes party.

Douglas was at the event with his son Cameron, who was about 13 at the time. In the book, Douglas alleges that Roberts had her arm around Cameron and was "kind of nuzzling him." Douglas, who admits he was drunk, claims Cameron looked stunned.
BRAD PITT SAYS HE CAN DRINK IN ‘RESTRAINED MANNER’ AFTER 7 SOBER YEARS, BUT EXPERT RAISES RED FLAG
"I told her, ‘Take your hands off my son and take that Golden Globe and stick it where the sun don’t shine,’" he wrote.
Douglas later apologized to Roberts and her boyfriend at the time, Kiefer Sutherland.
BRAD PITT ADMITS HE BEGAN DRINKING AGAIN AFTER YEARS OF SOBRIETY
"I sent Julia roses with an apology for my behavior, and then, back in the production office, I apologized to her and Kiefer in person," he wrote.
Fox News Digital has reached out to reps for Roberts for comment.
Douglas reveals secret affair with Lee Purcell
Lee Purcell and Michael Douglas had a secret affair in the 1970s. (Getty Images)
While filming "Adam at 6 A.M." early in his career, Douglas says he and his married co-star Lee Purcell became lovers.

"As filming progressed, my relationship with Lee changed and we became lovers," he wrote. "Our intimate relationship was complicated by the fact that she was married, and we had to keep it a secret from the cast, crew, the people in the town we were filming in, and of course her husband. It was a passionate affair that lasted through filming."

Purcell told Fox News Digital, "This story came as a complete surprise to me. I have fond memories of Michael and our time together. However, our recall appears to differ. First, I remember the process of searching for his character of Adam after having already been hired by Steve McQueen for the role of Jerri Jo. Secondly, we had a strictly professional relationship during filming. The personal one came much later."

Years later, while making "Romancing the Stone," Douglas also admits he had an affair with screenwriter Diane Thomas, who wrote the film. He says he and his first wife, Diandra, were both involved in extramarital relationships as their marriage deteriorated.
Diandra gave him a ‘rehab or divorce’ ultimatum
In the midst of his substance abuse and infidelity, Douglas said his first marriage to Diandra Luker eventually came to a head at the Beverly Wilshire Hotel.
After Diandra initially declined to stay with him at the hotel, Douglas called a woman he had been seeing. The woman came to his room, where they had drinks.
LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS
Douglas says Diandra unexpectedly returned, obtained a key from the front desk and walked in on them.
Michael Douglas and Diandra Luker married in 1977. (Ron Galella Collection via Getty Images)
"She gave me an ultimatum: ‘Rehab or divorce,’" he writes.

"The indiscretion, the drugs, the booze. I was in a constant state of temporary pleasure or temporary escape," he writes. "In my heart, I knew that I was heading down a very bad road at a very high speed, but I was trying my best to compartmentalize."
Douglas entered the Sierra Tucson rehabilitation clinic in Arizona in 1992 for treatment for alcohol and substance abuse.
PUT YOUR ENTERTAINMENT KNOWLEDGE TO THE TEST AND SEE HOW YOU SCORE
Douglas denies being a sex addict
Douglas says his rehab stay was later exploited by a tabloid.

He claims two fellow patients sold information about the program to a publication and then left treatment. According to Douglas, the story transformed his treatment for alcohol and drug abuse into a sensational headline portraying him as a sex addict.

"The story that was printed was utter bulls—," Douglas writes. "I had made mistakes, had moments I wasn’t proud of, made choices I wouldn’t have if I wasn’t high, but I was never a f---ing sex addict."
Douglas says the story damaged his reputation and continued to follow him in interviews for decades.
Douglas recalls partying with O.J. Simpson
Michael Douglas claims he once partied with O.J. Simpson. (Getty Images)
Douglas also writes about an encounter with O.J. Simpson and Rolling Stone co-founder Jann Wenner.

Douglas says he and Wenner encountered Simpson at a "Saturday Night Live" after-party. Wenner invited Simpson back to his apartment, where Simpson allegedly pulled out a rolled dollar bill and offered them cocaine.
"Jann and I were looking at each other — Are we really doing this with O.J. Simpson?" Douglas writes.
He also claims cocaine was readily available throughout Hollywood. Douglas says that at one major talent agency, a valet could allegedly replace a $100 bill left in a car with a packet of cocaine.
Fox News Digital has reached out to Wenner for comment.
Douglas describes a private evening with Princess Diana
Diana, Princess of Wales, talks to American actor Michael Douglas at the London premiere of the film "Wall Street" April 28, 1988. British actor Terence Stamp is in the center. (Getty Images)
Douglas writes that he spent a private evening with Princess Diana at a London screening of "Wall Street."
He says they sat beside each other during the film, with their hands occasionally touching on the shared armrest. Afterward, they spent time together at a private dinner away from the cameras.
"The truth was simple: she was in an unhappy marriage and wanted a different life," he writes.
He does not claim they had a romantic relationship, but describes their time together as "very special."
He recalls growing up afraid of Kirk Douglas
Actor Kirk Douglas and actor Michael Douglas in 2011 (Getty Images)
Douglas describes his father, Hollywood icon Kirk Douglas, as a powerful, but volatile presence.
"Kirk Douglas was my father, a flawed man with a ferocious temper and a burning ambition," he writes.
Douglas says his father’s behavior left him and his brother Joel frightened. He recalls Kirk saying, "I yell and scream because I care," while Douglas writes that Joel endured more of the abuse.
Douglas’ cancer was misdiagnosed for nine months
Douglas says doctors initially treated his persistent throat pain as an infection and prescribed multiple rounds of antibiotics.
A Canadian specialist eventually discovered a subtle swelling at the back of his tongue. A biopsy revealed squamous cell carcinoma.
"It’s stage IV cancer," the doctor told him, according to Douglas, who says the tumor was the size of a walnut.

Douglas writes that three doctors had missed the cancer and that he had been given the wrong diagnosis for nine months. He feared surgery would require removing part of his tongue and jaw, potentially ending his acting career.
His doctors publicly referred to the disease as throat cancer rather than tongue cancer because they feared reports about possible disfigurement would become sensationalized.
Douglas once tried to kidnap Cameron and force him into rehab
Douglas also describes the darkest years of his son Cameron’s addiction.
"When he was really strung out in New York, I decided I was going to kidnap him and force him into rehab," he wrote.

Douglas said that Cameron was addicted to cocaine and heroin, dealt methamphetamine and carried a Glock for protection. During one incident, Cameron flashed the weapon at a drugstore and was nearly shot by police.
Cameron Douglas and Michael Douglas attend the 2024 Vanity Fair Oscar Party at the Wallis Annenberg Center for the Performing Arts March 10, 2024, in Beverly Hills, Calif. (Variety via Getty Images)
At one point, Douglas says he arranged for two large men to help abduct Cameron and force him into rehab.
"When we came back, I asked to hold the leash. Cam figured it out. He looked at me, like, ‘Dad, how could you?’ Like I had broken his heart. Again."
Cameron realized what was happening and resisted, so Douglas threw the plan out of the window.

Cameron later served seven years in prison after a federal drug case. Douglas wrote that his son’s heroin relapse behind bars led a judge to add 4½ to his sentence, and Cameron also spent two years in solitary confinement.

title: New belly fat injection cuts dangerous fat surrounding organs by 12% in early human trial
summary: CBL-514 injection triggers apoptosis only in fat cells to reduce visceral fat by 12% in early trials, with implications for insulin resistance.
story: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. cautions that the nature of GLP drugs means there might be unknown side effects in a ‘Saturday in America’ town hall.
Early human trials of an experimental injection called CBL-514 have shown the potential for reducing deadly visceral fat.
Visceral fat, which sits deep inside the abdomen wrapped around internal organs, affects metabolism and influences insulin resistance. It can impact the development of type 2 diabetes.
Research published in March by the American Heart Association found that visceral fat had a stronger association with the risk of heart failure than body mass index (BMI).
YOUR WAISTLINE COULD REVEAL A HIDDEN HEART RISK YOUR BMI MISSES, MAJOR STUDY FINDS

The trials tested whether the injection could diminish visceral fat deposits. They were conducted by Dr. W. Timothy Garvey of the University of Alabama at Birmingham and Yu-Fang Ling of Caliway Biopharmaceuticals in New Taipei City, Taiwan.
Previous phase 2 trials had already shown that the drug could reduce subcutaneous fat, the layer of fat directly beneath the skin.
An experimental injection called CBL-514 has been shown to reduce visceral fat in early human trials. (iStock)
MRI scans from two phase 2 trials exhibited a decrease in visceral fat in participants who received the CBL-514 drug, while the visceral fat increased in those who received a placebo drug.
Participants who were given CBL-514 received injections into their lower abdomen every three weeks for up to 12 weeks, with doses of up to 600 milligrams.

The number of injections given to participants depended on the thickness of their abdominal fat.
As the fat layer decreased in volume, the number of injections also decreased.
The amount of injections that participants received depended upon the thickness of their abdominal fat. (iStock)
The CBL-514 injection selectively sparks apoptosis — a process that causes cells to self-destruct — but only in fat cells, leaving nearby cells unharmed.

Four weeks after the final treatment, the average volume of fat had lowered by 12.01% in the group given CBL-514, while it had increased by 5.68% in the group that received a placebo, SciTechDaily reported.
Participants who were given CBL-514 received injections into their lower abdomen every three weeks for up to 12 weeks — with doses of up to 600 milligrams. (iStock)
The potential cosmetic effects, such as a flatter stomach due to subcutaneous fat loss, are appealing to patients, Garvey acknowledged.

What’s even more important, he noted, however, is the decrease in body weight, improved blood pressure and cholesterol, and the loss of visceral fat that the injection can cause — as these factors impact overall health.

Liposuction, a common surgical cosmetic procedure, cannot remove visceral fat, and thus cannot reduce the health risks caused by a high amount of visceral fat.

title: Hidden clues could help predict a woman’s breast cancer risk years in advance
summary: An AI tool developed at NYU Langone Health analyzes years of 3D mammograms to predict breast cancer risk up to five years before a diagnosis.
story: AI technology is transforming breast cancer screening by assisting doctors in identifying women at higher risk years before cancer develops. Mount Sinai's Breast Surgery Director and author of 'The Breast Advice' Dr. Elisa Port highlights how AI uncovers hidden tumors and slashes false positive results, especially for women with dense breasts. This advancement aims to increase screening adherence among the 30-40% who currently don't get regular mammograms.
An artificial intelligence (AI) tool could help doctors predict a woman's risk of developing breast cancer years in advance, according to new research.

In a new study, published in the American Journal of Roentgenology, researchers at NYU Langone Health and its Perlmutter Cancer Center tested an AI model designed to estimate a woman's risk of developing breast cancer within five years.
The tool looks at several years of a woman's 3D mammograms to track changes in breast tissue over time, rather than looking only at the latest scan, according to the researchers.
NEW ALZHEIMER'S BLOOD TEST PREDICTS WHO IS LIKELY TO DEVELOP DEMENTIA IN 5 TO 10 YEARS
The model was developed using more than 313,000 mammograms from more than 161,000 women, according to the study.
An artificial intelligence (AI) tool could help doctors predict a woman's risk of developing breast cancer years in advance. (iStock)

Connie Lehman, a Massachusetts-based breast imaging specialist and professor of radiology at Harvard Medical School who was not involved in the study, told Fox News Digital that AI could help identify women whose increased risk might otherwise go unnoticed.

"For decades, as a doctor and breast imaging specialist, I have cared for women who were shocked by a breast cancer diagnosis," Lehman said. "Again and again, I heard: 'How can this be? No one in my family has had breast cancer.'"
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER
Traditional risk assessments can consider factors such as family history and genetic mutations, while AI can look for additional clues within a woman's breast tissue, according to Lehman.
The tool looks at several years of a woman's 3D mammograms to track changes in breast tissue over time. (iStock)
"A mammogram can tell us more than whether cancer is visible today — it can also provide information about a woman's risk of developing cancer in the years ahead," she said.
That information could eventually help doctors tailor breast cancer screening to a woman's individual risk, Lehman said.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Women identified as being at increased risk could discuss additional screening, such as MRI, with their health care providers, while women at average risk may continue with routine mammograms, according to Lehman.
The technology could also analyze mammograms a woman has already had, meaning the added risk information would not require another imaging exam or additional radiation, she noted.
Traditional risk assessments can consider factors such as family history and genetic mutations, while AI can look for additional clues in a woman's breast tissue, experts say. (iStock)
Lehman cautioned that an AI risk score is not a cancer diagnosis and cannot predict with certainty whether a woman will develop the disease.

"A higher score can prompt a conversation with your health care provider about additional screening and risk-reduction options," she said. "A lower score does not eliminate risk or replace regular mammography."
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
The NYU model remains a research tool and is not FDA-authorized for clinical use, according to Lehman.
The researchers also noted that more testing is needed. The study used mammograms from NYU Langone hospitals and imaging equipment from one manufacturer.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
The team plans to test the model using data from other medical centers and different 3D mammography systems, according to NYU Langone.
Fox News Digital reached out to the researchers for comment.

title: Silent inflammation could be damaging your body — and 5 habits may help keep it in check
summary: Jim LaValle reveals how the gut-immune-brain interface drives chronic inflammation, and why stress, blood sugar and environmental toxins play key roles.
story: Clinical pharmacist Jim LaValle breaks down how diet, stress, medications, blood sugar, environmental exposures and even overtraining may contribute to inflammation — and why the gut-brain connection matters.

Inflammation is a natural immune response that helps protect the body from injury and infection, but when it becomes chronic, it can pose a health threat, according to the National Institutes of Health.
Over time, chronic inflammation can contribute to rheumatoid arthritis, lupus, inflammatory bowel disease and cardiovascular disease.
Keeping the condition in check can help protect healthy tissues and support overall health, experts say.
POPULAR WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS MAY HELP PROTECT AGAINST A DEADLY DISEASE, DOCTOR SAYS
Jim LaValle, a clinical pharmacist and metabolic medicine expert based in Texas, told Fox News Digital that inflammation can be influenced by a variety of factors beyond injury or infection.
Inflammation is a natural immune response that helps protect the body from injury and infection, but chronic inflammation can damage healthy tissues and contribute to serious diseases. (iStock)

LaValle first pointed to the gut-immune-brain connection — the communication between gut microbes, the immune system and the central nervous system — as one pathway that can influence the body's inflammatory response.
Beyond gut health, he said several everyday lifestyle factors can play a role in preventing chronic inflammation.
DOCTORS SAY 8 FORGOTTEN HABITS COULD HELP FIGHT STRESS, OBESITY AND CHRONIC DISEASE
No. 1: Manage stress
Managing stress and anxiety can help support the gut-brain connection and keep inflammation in check, according to LaValle.
He pointed to cortisol, a hormone released in response to stress, which he said can "wreak havoc on your chemistry" when levels remain elevated.
Stress can "wreak havoc on your chemistry," the expert warned. (iStock)
Chronic stress can also affect the intestinal barrier, potentially allowing substances that would normally remain inside the gut to pass through more easily, LaValle said.
This increased intestinal permeability is sometimes called "leaky gut."
ZERO SUGAR, MORE PROBLEMS? STUDY REVEALS SURPRISING GUT HEALTH EFFECTS
"So, it turns out that if I'm stressed out a lot, I can be more prone to irritable bowel," LaValle said, as stress can trigger or worsen digestive symptoms in some people.
No. 2: Watch for food triggers
Diets high in sugar, fat and ultraprocessed foods can also affect gut health.
Paying attention to which foods trigger certain symptoms may help identify potential food sensitivities or intolerances, LaValle noted.
Paying attention to what kinds of food trigger certain reactions or sensitivities may help signal what is causing inflammation in the body. (iStock)
Symptoms such as bloating, rashes or discomfort after eating certain foods may signal a food-related reaction, although they can have other causes.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Certain medications, including antibiotics, may also alter the gut microbiome, but their effects vary depending on the drug and the individual, the expert said.
No. 3: Keep blood sugar in check
Maintaining healthy blood sugar levels is another important factor in managing inflammation, according to LaValle.
Maintaining healthy blood sugar levels is another important factor in managing inflammation. (iStock)
LaValle noted that conditions such as diabetes and insulin resistance are often associated with chronic inflammation.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Research suggests that GLP-1 medications, commonly prescribed for type 2 diabetes and obesity, may have anti-inflammatory effects, while scientists are investigating other potential benefits beyond weight loss and blood sugar control.
No. 4: Be aware of environmental exposures
The "exposome," or the environmental exposures people experience throughout their lives, can influence inflammation and the risk of chronic disease, according to the National Institutes of Health.
Microplastics could trigger inflammation signaling, according to the expert. (iStock)

LaValle pointed to emerging research on how environmental exposures — including "forever chemicals," microplastics, metals and pesticides — may affect weight, blood sugar regulation and other aspects of health.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
"A lot of us don't think about that kind of impact on our health and how that could trigger inflammation signaling," he added.
No. 5: Don’t over-train
Regular exercise supports overall health, but intense workouts without adequate recovery time can put additional stress on the body, LaValle cautioned.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"You’re not getting a good enough recovery," he said. "You’re training hard. And, in fact, you might be training hard every day to lower that cortisol, but you're not getting good recovery. And that could lead to silent inflammatory signaling as well."
Anyone who is concerned about chronic inflammation or is experiencing persistent symptoms should consult a doctor to determine the underlying cause and appropriate treatment.
Angelica Stabile is a lifestyle reporter for Fox News Digital.

title: Stomach-turning sexually transmitted infection is on the rise, and standard medicines are failing
summary: Shigella bacteria are becoming harder to treat as drug-resistant strains rise, and doctors warn Americans should be concerned but not panicked.
story: Speaking to Fox News Digital, Lenox Hill Hospital internist Michael Aziz discusses the increase in antibiotic-resistant shigella cases and explains why patients experiencing gastrointestinal symptoms should seek medical attention before taking over-the-counter medications.
A highly contagious gut infection that can spread during sex is becoming harder to treat as antibiotic-resistant strains become more common.

An April report from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention tracked nearly 17,000 shigella samples, which causes shigellosis that can bring on diarrhea, fever and abdominal cramps, collected between 2011 and 2023.

In 2023, 8.5% of shigella samples with resistance data were classified as extensively drug-resistant, or XDR — resistant to all five antibiotics in the CDC’s definition — compared with none from 2011 to 2015.
The findings point to a growing resistance problem, not a surge in overall infections, noted Dr. Tyler Evans, a California-based infectious disease physician and CEO of Wellness Equity Alliance.
HIGHLY CONTAGIOUS STOMACH BUG SPREADS FAST, HITTING CERTAIN PATIENTS HARDEST
"The infection is not surging. The bacteria are changing," Evans told Fox News Digital. "Case counts can hold steady while the treatment options quietly disappear."
The percentage of Shigella isolates classified as extensively drug-resistant rose to 8.5% in 2023, according to the CDC. (Leonie Asendorpf/picture alliance via Getty Images)
There is no FDA-approved oral antibiotic for XDR shigella, he said.
Shigella bacteria can spread when tiny amounts of stool reach someone's mouth, including through contaminated food or water, unwashed hands or sexual activity.
DANGEROUS DRUG-RESISTANT FUNGUS SPREADS ACROSS US, REACHING 27 STATES
"Shigella is not considered to be a typical sexually transmitted infection," Dr. Andi Toufexis, a Texas-based family medicine physician who specializes in sexual health, told Fox News Digital.
"However, this gastrointestinal bacteria can be spread through sex when one partner comes into contact with the other's fecal matter."
Most patients with extensively drug-resistant Shigella in the CDC analysis were adult men. (iStock)
Shigella is not new, and sexual transmission has been documented since the 1970s, Toufexis said. What is changing is the growing share of tested samples classified as XDR.
MICHIGAN REPORTS 2 DEATHS IN RARE PARASITE OUTBREAK THAT HAS SICKENED MORE THAN 11,000

The CDC report found that most people with XDR shigella were adult men. Sexual exposure data were not routinely collected, so the report could not establish exactly how each infection was contracted. But previous research has found sexual contact among men who have sex with men as an important transmission route.

Eighty-six percent of XDR patients were men with a median age of 41, and of those with a known HIV status, nearly half were living with HIV, Evans noted. People experiencing homelessness and those with weakened immune systems may also face heightened risks, he said.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Children younger than 5 are especially likely to get shigella, according to the CDC, and many outbreaks in the U.S. have been linked to childcare and schools. Earlier U.S. outbreaks primarily affected children and involved strains that were susceptible to antibiotics.
Washing hands before preparing food can help reduce the spread of Shigella.

According to the CDC report, 37.6% of patients with hospitalization data were hospitalized for the antibiotic-resistant infection. The CDC reported no deaths among the XDR cases analyzed and said infections may be undercounted because not all positive specimens were cultured or tested for resistance. Most patients with available travel histories reported no recent international travel, though travel information was missing for many.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
Evans said Americans should be "concerned, not panicked" about the infection.
Most shigella infections resolve on their own, Toufexis added, but severe illness may need treatment.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Dr. Michael Aziz, an internist at Lenox Hill Hospital in New York City and author of "The Perfect 10 Diet" and "The Ageless Revolution," urged people who suspect shigella to seek medical advice before taking antidiarrheal medicine such as Imodium.
"You want to flush out the bacteria, you want to get it out of your system," Aziz told Fox News Digital.
Experts advise people with Shigella not to take antidiarrheal medicines such as Imodium, which can slow the gut.

To reduce the chance of infection, doctors recommend washing hands, genitals and the anal area before and after sex, using condoms or dental dams and cleaning sex toys after each use. If you or a partner has diarrhea, avoid sex and wait at least two weeks after symptoms end before resuming, Toufexis said.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"Feeling better does not always mean that an infection is completely gone," she said.
Deirdre Bardolf is a lifestyle writer with Fox News Digital.

title: One type of sleep linked to dramatically lower risk of dementia, Parkinson's and 81 other diseases
summary: Greater REM sleep was linked to 80% lower Parkinson's risk and 46% lower dementia risk in a major study of over 95,000 adults tracked for years.
story: Erin Palinski-Wade, a New Jersey-based nutritionist and author of ‘The Sleepdemic Solution,’ confirmed that household surroundings and ambient neighborhood conditions can directly interfere with restfulness.
Not all stages of sleep are equal in terms of benefits for the brain.
Greater amounts of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep were associated with lower risks of 83 diseases, including dementia, Parkinson’s disease and heart failure, new research has shown.
Additionally, greater amounts of deep sleep were associated with lower risks of seven conditions.
THIS ONE QUESTION MAY REVEAL WHETHER YOUR BODY IS GETTING THE REST IT NEEDS, STUDY FINDS

That’s according to a study of 95,559 adults who wore wrist accelerometers continuously for seven consecutive days and nights. Researchers in China used deep-learning algorithms to analyze REM sleep, deep sleep, light sleep, total sleep duration, wakefulness after sleep onset and sleep irregularity.
They then looked at health records to assess associations with more than 1,000 diseases over a nearly nine-year follow-up period.
Greater amounts of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep were associated with lower risks of 83 diseases, including dementia, Parkinson’s disease and heart failure, new research has shown. (iStock)
Greater REM sleep was associated with a significantly lower risk of several diseases, including Parkinson’s (80% lower relative risk), dementia (46% lower risk) and heart failure (26% lower risk).
Greater deep sleep was associated with lower risks of seven conditions, including Type 2 diabetes and major depressive disorder.
MORE NAPS, HIGHER RISK? RESEARCH LINKS DAYTIME SLEEP TO HEALTH WARNINGS IN AGING ADULTS

Sleep duration was also found to be highly linked to disease outcome. Six to eight hours per night was found to be the "sweet spot" associated with the lowest risk for 69 diseases. In contrast, sleeping fewer than five hours per night was linked to an increased risk of 37 health conditions.

The study also found that greater night-to-night sleep irregularity and more wakefulness during the night were associated with higher risks of several conditions, including anxiety and substance use disorders.
The findings were published Sept. 17 in the journal PLOS Medicine.
Disrupted sleep may sometimes be an early warning sign of disease rather than simply a cause, a sleep expert noted. (iStock)

"I think what is important is the total duration of sleep, and the percentage that REM takes up," Oki Ishikawa, M.D., pulmonary, critical care and sleep medicine expert at Northwell’s Northern Westchester Hospital, told Fox News Digital.
"The average percentage of REM sleep in this study population was about 20%, and generally 20-25% is considered normal per sleep cycle."
5-STEP SLEEP RESET COULD PROMOTE HEALTHY WEIGHT LOSS, NUTRITIONIST SAYS
Ishikawa, who was not involved in the study, said he does not believe that a higher amount of REM sleep alone will necessarily lower the risk.

"Normal sleep pattern and duration are associated with aspects like maintenance of good immune function and memory, so I think the important message here is to try and get a sufficient amount of sleep in general," Ishikawa sai.
Researchers used deep-learning algorithms to analyze REM sleep, deep sleep, light sleep, total sleep duration, wakefulness after sleep onset and sleep irregularity. (iStock)
Disrupted sleep may sometimes be an early warning sign of disease rather than simply a cause, according to Dr. Chelsie Rohrscheib, head sleep expert at Wesper, a sleep analysis company in New York.

"Conditions such as Parkinson’s disease, dementia and heart failure can begin affecting sleep years before they are diagnosed," Rohrscheib, who also was not involved in the research, told Fox News Digital.
"At the same time, poor sleep may contribute to disease progression, so the relationship likely works both ways."
DIETITIAN REVEALS SIMPLE EATING STRATEGY FOR BETTER SLEEP — AND ONE HABIT TO AVOID
The researchers noted some limitations of the study. Because it was observational, it could only show an association and could not prove that increasing REM or deep sleep directly prevents disease.
"Sleep was measured for only one week using a wrist device, which is less accurate than a clinical sleep study for identifying sleep stages," Rohrscheib said.
"Poor sleep may contribute to disease progression, so the relationship likely works both ways," an expert said. (iStock)
"Some health information was collected years earlier, medications that can affect sleep were not fully considered and some medical diagnoses may have been missed."

As the participants were all from the UK Biobank, the study population was also less diverse and generally healthier than the overall population, so the findings may not apply equally to everyone, Rohrscheib noted.
CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES
"Overall, changes in sleep may provide important clues about underlying health, but this study cannot determine whether poor sleep is a cause, an early symptom or both," she concluded.
Rohrscheib also cautioned that while wrist-worn sleep trackers are generally good at estimating sleep stages, they are not 100% accurate.
CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER
"Without a formal in-lab sleep study, it's impossible to know how much time the participants spent in REM and other sleep stages," she said.
More research is needed to determine whether increasing REM or deep sleep can help prevent certain diseases, the researchers said.
"If you get about seven to nine hours of uninterrupted sleep, you most likely have the opportunity to cycle through REM in a sufficient way."
Future studies could also explore whether the relationship between sleep stages and disease risk varies by age, sex, overall health and other individual characteristics.

Both experts recommended following general sleep hygiene practices, such as maintaining an optimal environment (dark, cool and quiet), keeping a consistent sleep schedule and avoiding sleep-disrupting substances such as alcohol and caffeine.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"If you have other sleep pathologies like sleep apnea … treating that would be a great way to optimize the amount of REM sleep," Ishikawa advised.
TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ
While it can be difficult to measure REM sleep without a wearable, he said the best gauge is whether one feels refreshed upon waking and doesn’t feel sleepy during the day.
"If you get about seven to nine hours of uninterrupted sleep, you most likely have the opportunity to cycle through REM in a sufficient way."
